Report of the surgical scheduling manager to the Access Standards Group, Millward General Hospital, 4 March 2026, concerning a cancelled hemiarthroplasty and whether the 28-day rebooking guarantee applies.

The patient, a 74-year-old woman listed for an elective left hip hemiarthroplasty, was admitted to Ward 5 at 18:30 on Monday 23 February 2026 under the day-before admission pathway. Her procedure was scheduled first on the Tuesday 24 February morning list. At 22:10 on the Monday evening, the on-call anaesthetist recorded in the notes: "No level 2 bed available post-op tomorrow; critical care full with two pending admissions from ED. Not safe to proceed without HDU bed. Cancel for tomorrow, rebook." The patient was discharged home on Tuesday morning and has been waiting since. On 2 March the family asked for a date, and the booking office replied that the next available list was 14 April.

The hospital's Cancelled Operations Standard, version 5, states the rule at paragraph 2: "A patient whose operation is cancelled by the hospital on the day of surgery for a non-clinical reason must be offered a new date for the operation within 28 days of the cancellation, and the offer must be made within seven days." Paragraph 3 sets out the exception: "Paragraph 2 does not apply where the cancellation is for a clinical reason, or where the patient cancels or does not attend." Paragraph 4 addresses a neighbouring situation and provides that where a patient is cancelled before the day of surgery, for instance by a letter sent the week before, the patient is rebooked in turn according to clinical priority and waiting time, and the 28-day guarantee does not apply.

Version 5's definitions at paragraph 6 provide that "non-clinical reason" includes the unavailability of a ward, critical care or theatre bed, a shortage of staff, theatre list overrun, equipment failure and administrative error, and that "clinical reason" means a reason arising from the patient's own condition, such as an intercurrent infection, an abnormal test result or a change in the patient's fitness for anaesthesia, as documented by the responsible clinician. The definitions add that the characterisation of the reason is determined by these definitions and not by the wording chosen in the clinical entry.

The standard was amended by Amendment 5.1, approved by the Access Standards Group on 10 November 2025 and effective 1 January 2026. Before the amendment, "on the day of surgery" was defined as the calendar day on which the operation was scheduled. Amendment 5.1 replaced that definition with: "on the day of surgery means at any time after the patient has been admitted for the procedure, or on the calendar day on which the operation was scheduled, whichever is earlier." The amendment note explains that day-before admissions had previously fallen outside the guarantee.

The booking office's view, recorded in the file, is that the cancellation was made on the Monday evening, not on the Tuesday, and that the anaesthetist's entry describes a safety judgement, so the guarantee does not apply and the patient is rebooked in turn. The manager asks the group to determine the point.

Section 5, which the pharmacist notes as a neighbouring provision, deals with medicines started on the ward that are to be stopped at discharge, which are not supplied at all.

The rota coordinator wants to fill a gap on the acute medical take and has asked for the earliest shift start the doctor can be given after 09:00 on Friday. The options on the table are a Friday evening twilight shift starting at 20:00, a Saturday day shift at 08:00, a Sunday early shift at 07:00, a Sunday night at 20:00 and the Monday day shift at 08:00. The doctor has said she would take the Saturday shift if it is allowed, because she is saving for a course.

The applicable document is the Junior Doctor Working Pattern Rules, version 3, which the trust adopted in 2023 and which the guardian polices. Section 4 provides the general rule: "Between the end of a shift and the beginning of the doctor's next shift there must be a rest period of at least eleven hours." Section 5 provides an exception for emergency call-back: "Where a doctor who is resting is called back to the hospital for an emergency, the call-back does not count as a shift for the purposes of section 4 and does not restart the rest period, provided the call-back does not exceed two hours." Section 6 deals with on-call from home and states that a period of on-call from home is not a shift, that only time spent attending the hospital during it counts as work, and that on-call periods do not form part of a run of shifts.

Section 8 contains the definitions. A "night shift" is "a shift of which at least three hours fall between 23:00 and 06:00". A "run of night shifts" means "three or more night shifts on consecutive calendar days". Section 9 records amendments. Amendment 3.1, effective 3 February 2026, inserted a new paragraph into section 4: "Following a run of night shifts, the rest period before the next shift is forty-six hours, measured from the end of the final night shift in the run, in place of the eleven hours in the first paragraph of this section." The accompanying note explains that the eleven-hour minimum was found inadequate after runs of nights.

The rota coordinator has pointed out that the doctor did attend the hospital briefly on Wednesday afternoon, between her second and third nights, for ninety minutes at the request of the medical registrar to help with a deteriorating patient, which was logged as an emergency call-back. The coordinator's own reading is that this call-back is what determines the rest calculation.

question.instructions: Apply the Junior Doctor Working Pattern Rules as amended and select the earliest permitted shift start for the doctor from the options considered.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-shadow-2
provenance.rationale: Each of the Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday shifts (20:30–09:00) has more than three hours between 23:00 and 06:00, so they are night shifts on three consecutive calendar days and form a run of night shifts. Amendment 3.1, in force since February 2026, requires forty-six hours' rest from the end of the final night shift at 09:00 on Friday, which is 07:00 on Sunday. The Monday on-call from home is not a shift and is not part of the run. The ninety-minute Wednesday call-back does not count as a shift and does not restart the rest period under section 5, so it neither breaks the run nor alters the calculation.
provenance.why_hard: The headline eleven-hour rule gives Friday 20:00, the doctor's preference and the coordinator's focus on the call-back both distract, and the forty-six-hour rule sits in an amendment whose trigger depends on the night-shift definition.

Note for the Associate Dean (Education), Faculty of Arts, Corwen University, from the faculty registrar, 2 November 2026, on a module change request received in teaching week 5.

A second-year undergraduate on the BA English programme has asked to swap the optional module ENG2310 Victorian Fiction for ENG2380 Modern Drama. The request arrived through the module change portal on Monday 26 October 2026, which is the start of teaching week 5 of the autumn term (week 1 began Monday 28 September). The student's stated reason is a timetable clash: the ENG2310 seminar she attends now clashes with the language class she takes as a co-curricular option through the Language Centre.

The Module Change Regulations, 2026/27 edition, state the rule at regulation 3: "A student may change an optional module until the end of teaching week 3 of the term in which the module begins. Requests after that point are refused." Regulation 4 sets out an exception: "Where a timetable clash arises from a university change, the student may change module until the end of teaching week 4, and the faculty may in addition waive the deadline to the extent the clash made an earlier request impossible." Regulation 5 is concerned with a neighbouring situation, withdrawal from a module without replacement, which is permitted until the end of teaching week 8 with a W grade recorded, and which the registrar mentions because the student has said she would rather drop the module than keep the clash.

The definitions in regulation 8 state that "teaching week" means a numbered week in the published term calendar, that "university change" means "a change to the published timetable made by the Timetabling Office after the timetable is released, including a change of room, day or time for a session", and that "changes arising from the student's own selection, including a change of seminar group requested by the student, are not university changes". Regulation 9 records that the 2026/27 edition replaced "teaching week 2" with "teaching week 3" in regulation 3; the 2025/26 edition had the earlier deadline. The regulation 4 deadline of week 4 is unchanged.

The registrar has checked the timetabling records. The ENG2310 seminar groups were published on 14 September. The student was originally allocated to seminar group B (Thursdays 11:00), which does not clash with the language class. On 8 October, in teaching week 2, she used the self-service seminar swap tool to move to group D (Tuesdays 14:00), which the tool allows students to do freely; the portal log records the change as student-initiated. The Timetabling Office made no change to either group's day, time or room. The Language Centre class, which the student describes as "compulsory for my future year abroad", was itself moved by the Language Centre on 1 October from Wednesday to Tuesday at 14:00, and it is that move that produced the clash with group D; the Language Centre is not part of the Timetabling Office and its classes are not on the published academic timetable.

The registrar's provisional view is that the request must be refused, and the Associate Dean is asked to confirm.

question.instructions: Under the Module Change Regulations 2026/27, can the student's module change request be granted? Answer yes or no.

criteria.true: The regulations permit the module change to be granted.
criteria.false: The regulations require the request to be refused.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-shadow-2
provenance.rationale: The request was made in teaching week 5, after the amended week-3 deadline in regulation 3. The exception in regulation 4 requires a university change, defined as a change made by the Timetabling Office to the published timetable; the clash here arose from the student's own seminar swap and from a Language Centre move, and the definitions exclude student-initiated changes while the Language Centre class is not on the published timetable. Even the extended week-4 deadline would have passed. Withdrawal under regulation 5 is a different remedy and does not permit a change of module.
provenance.why_hard: There is a real, externally caused clash and the week-4 exception exists; the answer depends on who made the change and on the timing, both buried in the timetabling records.

Report from the Examinations Office at Dunmere University to the Deputy Registrar, 24 April 2026, concerning a request to defer a written examination on grounds of religious observance.

The student, a final-year undergraduate in Chemistry, has asked that her CHM3102 examination, scheduled for Thursday 21 May 2026 at 09:30, be moved to an alternative sitting because the date coincides with a religious festival she observes. The request was received on the Examinations Office's deferral form on Monday 20 April 2026. The summer examination period for 2025/26 runs from Monday 18 May to Friday 5 June 2026 as published in the academic calendar.

The Examination Arrangements Policy, 2025/26 edition, provides at section 6.1 that "a student may request an alternative sitting of an examination on grounds of religious observance, and the request will be granted where an alternative sitting can be arranged within the examination period, provided the request is received by the Examinations Office no later than four weeks before the first day of the examination period". Section 6.2 sets out an exception: "Where the examination timetable is published later than four weeks before the first day of the examination period, a request under 6.1 is accepted if received within ten working days of publication of the timetable." Section 6.3 concerns deferral on medical grounds, which is handled by the Mitigating Circumstances Committee and is not subject to the four-week deadline, and the office notes that the student mentioned in passing a recent period of illness but has not applied on that basis.

Section 9 contains definitions. A request is "received" when the completed deferral form is logged by the Examinations Office; emails to a personal tutor or department are not requests. "Publication of the timetable" means "the date the personal examination timetables are released to students on the portal"; the provisional master timetable circulated to departments is not publication. "Working days" exclude weekends and the closure days listed in the calendar, of which there are none in April or May 2026.

Section 11 records amendments. Amendment 2025/26-1, effective 1 September 2025, changed the period in section 6.1 from "four weeks" to "six weeks". The Examinations Office's own internal checklist still carries the old wording, which the office is correcting. Section 6.2 was not changed by the amendment and still refers to four weeks.

The relevant dates are these. The provisional master timetable was circulated to departments on 20 March 2026. Personal timetables were released to students on the portal on Thursday 16 April 2026, which the office acknowledges was later than intended because of a room-booking system fault; in previous years the release has been in early April. The student emailed her personal tutor on 17 April to say she would need to move the exam and completed the deferral form on 20 April. The office can arrange an alternative sitting on Tuesday 26 May at 09:30 with an invigilator. The Deputy Registrar is asked whether the policy requires the request to be granted.

question.instructions: Under the Examination Arrangements Policy as amended, must the Examinations Office grant the student's request for an alternative sitting? Answer yes or no.

criteria.true: The policy requires the request to be granted.
criteria.false: The policy does not require the request to be granted; it may be refused as out of time or otherwise.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-shadow-2
provenance.rationale: Under amended section 6.1 the ordinary deadline is six weeks before 18 May, i.e. 6 April, and the request was received on 20 April, so it is late under 6.1. But personal timetables were published on 16 April, later than four weeks before the examination period, which triggers the exception in 6.2 (unamended, still four weeks); the request was received two working days after publication, within ten working days. An alternative sitting on 26 May is within the examination period, so the request must be granted.
provenance.why_hard: The amendment lengthening the deadline and the office's own checklist both push toward 'out of time', and the exception is triggered only by the portal release date, not the earlier departmental circulation.

Memo from the Postgraduate Admissions Office at Selwick University to the Head of Fees, 3 July 2026, on an application for the alumni fee discount.

An applicant holding an offer for the MSc Environmental Management, starting September 2026, has requested the alumni discount on her tuition fee. Her application form lists two prior qualifications: a BA (Hons) in Geography awarded in 2021 by Northcote College, and a Postgraduate Certificate in Sustainability Leadership awarded by Selwick University in 2024 after a one-year part-time programme in the Business School. She holds no scholarship for the MSc. She writes that she "graduated from Selwick two years ago" and that the admissions webpage says alumni receive 20% off postgraduate fees.

The Fee Discounts Policy, 2026/27 edition, provides at section 3.1 the rule: "A graduate of the University is entitled to a discount of 20% on the tuition fee for a postgraduate taught programme." Section 3.2 provides the exception: "The alumni discount is not awarded in combination with any scholarship or bursary funded by the University that exceeds 20% of the fee; where both would apply, the student receives whichever is greater." Section 3.3 provides a staff discount of 50% for members of staff on contracts of at least 0.5 FTE, which is awarded separately and cannot be combined with the alumni discount; the applicant is not a member of staff. Section 3.4 states that discounts are applied at enrolment on production of the award certificate.

Section 5 sets out definitions. "Graduate of the University" means "a person on whom the University has conferred a degree, that is a bachelor's, integrated master's, master's or doctoral award, by its own authority or under a validation agreement listed in Schedule 1". The same section provides that "Postgraduate Certificate and Postgraduate Diploma awards, and certificates of attendance or completion for short courses, are not degrees for the purposes of this policy".

Section 7 records amendments. Amendment 2026/27-A, effective 1 August 2026 for entrants from September 2026, extends section 3.1: "A person on whom Fallowmead College has conferred a bachelor's degree under its validation agreement with the University is treated as a graduate of the University for the purposes of this section." Fallowmead College is listed in Schedule 1 as a validated partner since 2015. Northcote College is not in Schedule 1; the admissions officer confirms Northcote's degrees are validated by a different university.

The Business School's records confirm the applicant completed the Postgraduate Certificate with distinction in July 2024 and attended the graduation ceremony that November, at which certificate holders are presented alongside degree holders. The applicant has attached a photograph of her certificate and the ceremony programme listing her name. The Head of Fees is asked to decide whether the alumni discount applies.

question.instructions: Under the Fee Discounts Policy as amended, is the applicant entitled to the alumni discount on her MSc fee? Answer yes or no.

criteria.true: The applicant is a graduate of the University for the policy's purposes and the discount applies.
criteria.false: The applicant is not entitled to the alumni discount.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-shadow-2
provenance.rationale: The discount requires a graduate of the University, defined as a person on whom a degree was conferred by the University or under a Schedule 1 validation agreement. The Postgraduate Certificate from Selwick is expressly not a degree under section 5, however it was celebrated at the ceremony. The BA was awarded by Northcote College, which is not in Schedule 1 and is validated elsewhere; Amendment 2026/27-A extends the definition only to Fallowmead College graduates. She therefore holds no qualifying degree and the discount does not apply.
provenance.why_hard: The applicant did complete a Selwick award and 'graduated' at its ceremony, and the amendment about validated colleges looks like it might reach her BA; both fail on the definitions.

Case summary prepared by the School Academic Integrity Officer, School of Business, Ravensdale University, for the integrity panel meeting of 12 November 2026.

The case concerns a level 5 (second-year) student on the BSc Marketing programme and a 2,000-word individual essay for module MKT2050, submitted on 23 October 2026, in the first term of the student's second year. The module leader referred the essay after the similarity report showed three passages, totalling 8% of the essay's word count after exclusion of the bibliography and quoted material, that reproduce text from two published journal articles without quotation marks or citation. The student's response, given at the initial meeting on 4 November, was that she had pasted the passages into her notes while reading and lost track of which were her own words; she did not deny the passages were copied. The module leader's referral form ticks the box "collusion suspected" because a second student on the module submitted an essay on the same topic, but the officer has compared the two essays and found no shared text; the second student's essay is not referred.

The Academic Integrity Procedure, 2026/27 edition, defines at section 2 the outcomes available to a school panel. For a first offence of plagiarism the outcome under section 4.1 is a mark of zero for the assessment with a right to resubmit for a capped mark. Section 4.2 provides that a second or subsequent offence results in a mark of zero for the module. Section 4.3 provides that cases involving collusion, contract cheating or falsified data are referred to the University Disciplinary Committee rather than determined by the school panel. Section 4.4 provides the exception: "Where the student is at level 4 and in their first term of study, and the unattributed material does not exceed 10% of the assessment, the panel records a finding of poor academic practice, imposes no penalty, and requires the student to complete the academic writing tutorial." Section 6 defines "first offence" as a case where the student has no prior recorded finding of plagiarism, poor academic practice or collusion on the student record, and defines "unattributed material" as the percentage shown on the similarity report after exclusion of bibliography and quoted material.

Section 8 records amendments. Amendment 2026/27-1, effective 1 September 2026, replaced the words "at level 4 and in their first term of study" in section 4.4 with "at level 4 or level 5 and in the first term of the academic year in which the assessment is submitted". The Senate paper explains that the poor-practice route was being denied to direct-entry and progressing students who had never received writing training.

The student record shows no prior findings of any kind. The student did not take MKT1010, the first-year module in which the academic writing tutorial is embedded, because she transferred into year two from a foundation programme at another institution in September 2026. The officer's checklist, printed in August, still shows the pre-amendment wording of section 4.4. The panel is asked to determine the outcome.

question.instructions: Apply the Academic Integrity Procedure as amended and select the outcome the panel should record.

criteria.zero_for_module: Zero for the module under section 4.2.
criteria.refer_to_disciplinary_committee: Refer to the University Disciplinary Committee under section 4.3.
criteria.zero_for_assessment_resubmit_capped: Zero for the assessment with capped resubmission under section 4.1.
criteria.poor_academic_practice_no_penalty: Finding of poor academic practice, no penalty, writing tutorial required.
criteria.no_finding_dismiss: Dismiss the case with no finding.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-shadow-2
provenance.rationale: The student is at level 5 and the essay was submitted on 23 October 2026, in the first term of the academic year; under section 4.4 as amended from 1 September 2026 the poor-practice route now covers level 5 students in that term. The unattributed material is 8%, within the 10% limit, and the student has no prior findings. The collusion box on the referral is unsupported because the officer found no shared text, so section 4.3 is not engaged. The copying is admitted, so dismissal is not available; the outcome is poor academic practice with no penalty and the tutorial.
provenance.why_hard: Section 4.1 is the standard first-offence outcome and the officer's printed checklist still shows the old level-4-only wording, while the ticked collusion box invites a referral upward.

Briefing for the Scholarships Committee, Hartwell University, 8 July 2026, prepared by the Student Funding Office on the continuation of a Vice-Chancellor's Excellence Scholarship into year three.

The scholar is a year-two student on the BSc Physics programme who holds a Vice-Chancellor's Excellence Scholarship worth 4,000 a year. The scholarship's continuation is decided each July on the year's results. The student also had a case before the Mitigating Circumstances Committee in May relating to a bereavement, and that committee accepted the circumstances and granted her a first-attempt resit of PHY2200 without capping.

The Scholarship Regulations, 2025/26 edition, set the continuation rule at section 5.1: "A scholarship continues into the following year of study where the scholar's year average is 60 or above." Section 5.2 provides the exception: "Where the year average is 55 or above but below the threshold in 5.1, and the Mitigating Circumstances Committee has accepted circumstances affecting the year, the scholarship continues at 50% of its value." Section 5.3 provides that where the year average is below 55 the scholarship is terminated, and section 5.4 that a scholarship is terminated at any time on a finding of misconduct by the University Disciplinary Committee, which does not arise here.

Section 7 defines "year average" as "the credit-weighted mean of the marks obtained at the first attempt in each module of the year, before any resit or reassessment, as confirmed by the exam board", and states that marks from uncapped resits granted for mitigating circumstances are recorded on the transcript but do not replace first-attempt marks for the purposes of this section. Section 9 records Amendment 2025/26-2, effective 1 June 2026, which added to section 5.1: "For scholars in year two or later, the threshold in this section is 58 rather than 60." The amendment note states that it applies to continuation decisions taken in July 2026 onward.

The exam board confirmed the following first-attempt marks on 30 June 2026: PHY2100 Quantum Mechanics (20 credits) 64; PHY2200 Electromagnetism (20 credits) 41; PHY2300 Thermal Physics (20 credits) 62; PHY2400 Mathematical Methods (20 credits) 59; PHY2500 Laboratory (20 credits) 66; PHY2600 Computational Physics (20 credits) 58. The uncapped resit of PHY2200 is scheduled for August, and the department expects a mark in the 60s. The Funding Office's spreadsheet, which projects the resit at 65, shows a "projected average" of 62.3 and the office's draft letter, prepared before the exam board met, recommended full continuation on that basis. The scholar's personal tutor has written separately urging the committee to "at least continue at half value given the bereavement".

question.instructions: Apply the Scholarship Regulations as amended and select the correct continuation decision for the July 2026 review.

criteria.continue_full_value: Continue the scholarship at full value into year three.
criteria.continue_half_value: Continue the scholarship at 50% of its value under section 5.2.
criteria.defer_until_resit_result: Defer the decision until the August resit mark is confirmed.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-shadow-2
provenance.rationale: All six modules carry 20 credits, so the year average is the plain mean of the first-attempt marks: (64 + 41 + 62 + 59 + 66 + 58) / 6 = 350 / 6 = 58.33. The uncapped resit does not replace the first-attempt mark under section 7, so deferral is pointless and the 62.3 projection is not the regulatory figure. The scholar is in year two, so Amendment 2025/26-2 sets the threshold at 58, which 58.33 meets; the scholarship continues at full value, and the half-value exception is not reached.
provenance.why_hard: The 41 in one module and the accepted mitigating circumstances make the half-value route look like the intended one, and the reader must both compute the weighted mean and know the amended threshold to see that full continuation applies.
